full_text:
A Dunfermline pub has continued its impressive streak at the Loo of the Year Awards by winning for the second year in a row.
The Guildhall and Linen Exchange once again proved it has thrones fit for a king with a platinum grading in the awards, which recognise high standards in public toilet facilities across the UK.
It's no flash in the pan for the Wetherspoon pub, as six awards in the last nine years show that they're anything but bog standard.
Manager Michele Park was flushed with success. She said: "We are delighted with the grading. Staff at the pub ensure the toilets are in excellent condition at all times and it is great that this has been recognised by the inspectors."
Staff were left relieved after judges awarded the loos with a platinum award after an unannounced visit.
The toilets are judged against numerous criteria, including décor and maintenance, cleanliness, accessibility, hand washing and drying equipment and overall management.
Rest assured, once patrons of the High Street watering hole find the toilets, they are up to award-winning standard.
Becky Wall, managing director of the Loo of the Year Awards, confirmed the toilets scrub up nicely.
She said: "The toilets at The Guildhall and Linen Exchange have been independently assessed against the Loo of the Year Awards’ 101 criteria, recognising the standard of the facilities, their cleanliness, maintenance, and overall presentation.
"The pub thoroughly deserves its platinum grading."

title: Cavite heat index hits 43°C, eases to 35°C - Daily Tribune

full_text:
The heat index at Sangley Point in Cavite City reached a dangerous 43 degrees Celsius on Thursday, 19 November, before dropping to 35°C on Friday, according to the latest monitoring report of the Department of Science and Technology–Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (DOST-PAGASA).
The Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (RDRRMC) CALABARZON Emergency Operations Center released the five-day computed heat index and two-day forecast on Friday, 20 November, showing a decline in readings across several monitoring stations.
The 43°C recorded at Sangley Point falls under PAGASA's danger classification of 42°C to 51°C, where heat cramps and heat exhaustion are likely and prolonged exposure may lead to heat stroke.
Despite the decline, several areas continued to experience heat index levels requiring extreme caution.
Mulanay, Quezon recorded the highest heat index in the region on Friday at 36°C, followed by Sangley Point at 35°C, Alabat, Quezon at 34°C, and Ambulong in Tanauan City, Batangas at 33°C.
The monitoring stations in Los Baños, Laguna registered 32°C; Tayabas City and Infanta, Quezon recorded 31°C each; Indang, Cavite posted 29°C; and Tanay, Rizal recorded 24°C.
Earlier in the monitoring period, Mulanay also experienced danger-level heat, reaching 42°C on 18 November.
For Saturday, 21 November, PAGASA forecasts a heat index of 35°C in Mulanay, 34°C in Sangley Point and Alabat, and 33°C in several other monitoring areas.
On Sunday, 22 November, Mulanay is expected to reach 36°C, while Sangley Point and Alabat may register 35°C.
PAGASA classifies heat index readings between 33°C and 41°C as extreme caution, with possible heat cramps and heat exhaustion. Continued exposure and strenuous activity may increase the risk of heat-related illness.
The heat index measures how hot conditions feel to the human body when air temperature and relative humidity are combined.
The public is advised to limit prolonged outdoor activities, drink sufficient water, and take precautions against heat-related illnesses, particularly during periods of elevated heat index readings.
